glosses: eat or bring an indefinite entity
senses.definition: Form one of nine declared third-singular or first-plural eat/bring Absolute predicates and require the matching overt bare indefinite object.

idiomatic: someone eats or brings an admitted entity

grammatical_features: Three predicate stems each have third-singular, inclusive first-plural, and exclusive first-plural cells.
Third-singular clauses require an overt lexical subject before the predicate; first-plural clauses omit an independent pronoun.

translation: Eat is limited to consuming food; bring is accompanied transfer toward a contextual destination.
grammar: The a/o bridges are contact abstractions. Final ii of miičii- deletes before o, yielding miičo-, while other stems concatenate transparently.
design: The construction joins regional suppletion, valency, and participant architecture to Hebrew-derived food, family, and person vocabulary in complete ordinary clauses.

inputs.form: transitive stem with AI-shaped inflection plus overt indefinite object
nine finite cells plus declared subjects and objects
inputs.contribution: Contact class bridges, ii truncation, exact host inventory, and narrative firewall.

operations.description: Retain the source requirement that the Absolute object be overt and indefinite and use AI-shaped participant inflection.
Use contact a for TA and o for TI before the number ending in every declared cell.
Delete stem-final ii in miičii- immediately before contact o, so miičii-o surfaces miičo rather than creating a four-vowel sequence.
Close subjects, objects, roles, and meanings to the inventory stated here.

formation.formation_process: Manual nine-cell contact construction based on cited source architecture and three independently reviewed contact stems.
formation.design_alignment: Creates genuinely usable co-parent domestic grammar without pretending to inherit the exact mixed forms from either source language.

provenance.generation_note: Codex manually selected every stem, cell, morphophonemic repair, subject/object inventory, meaning, and exclusion; tooling only validates the declaration.

construction_spec.function: Form a bounded ordinary Absolute clause for eating an admitted food or bringing an admitted entity.
construction_spec.formalism: 3SG: SUBJECT STEM~CLASS~w OBJECT; 1PL.INCL: kə~STEM~CLASS~hna OBJECT; 1PL.EXCL: nə~STEM~CLASS~hna OBJECT
host_classes: miičii- plus bare lexem or pri
peešəw- plus bare adam or yeled
peel- plus bare lexem, pri, or tiihinčəw
ordering: overt lexical subject only in third-singular clauses
allomorphy: TA uses contact a; TI uses contact o.
miičii loses final ii before o: miičii-o becomes miičo.
peešəw-a and peel-o concatenate without further change.
restrictions: Third-singular subjects are limited to bare adam, yeled, or em and cannot be omitted.
Objects are mandatory, bare, nondefinite, and selected by the declared stem class; admitted count objects are singular.
No definite, plural, possessed, incorporated, omitted, recipient, goal, source, or route object is licensed.
No tense, aspect, modality, polarity, imperative, direct/inverse, proximate/obviative, wayyiqtol, weqatal, foreground, consequence, or center-shift value is supplied.
counterexamples: miičii with adam or yeled is outside this tranche.
peešəw with lexem and peel with yeled are class mismatches.
Untruncated miičiio forms are invalid in this construction.
Two third-person animate participants remain recoverable only through overt noun order; this is not narrative participant tracking.

cells.meaning: a stated third-singular subject eats an overt indefinite admitted food
we including you eat an overt indefinite admitted food
we excluding you eat an overt indefinite admitted food
a stated third-singular subject brings an overt indefinite admitted animate entity
we including you bring an overt indefinite admitted animate entity
we excluding you bring an overt indefinite admitted animate entity
a stated third-singular subject brings an overt indefinite admitted inanimate entity
we including you bring an overt indefinite admitted inanimate entity
we excluding you bring an overt indefinite admitted inanimate entity

change_note: Created nine closed eat/bring Absolute cells with a contact-specific hiatus repair and explicit ordinary role order.

senses.definition: An exact noun-property phrase describing one indefinite child as physically small.

grammatical_features: The noun precedes the invariant property word.
The construction has exactly one admitted noun-property pair.

translation: Small refers only to physical size, not age, affection, insignificance, or social status.
grammar: No Hebrew gender agreement, article, plural, possession, degree, or general adjective class is licensed.
design: The phrase preserves a recognizably Hebrew noun-property order while deliberately regularizing agreement inside the contact language.

operations.description: Place contact katan after bare yeled and license no other host or interpretation.

formation.design_alignment: Advances a protected song image through living Hebrew-derived syntax while refusing to declare a general adjective system from one phrase.

provenance.generation_note: Codex manually selected the order, meaning, agreement policy, and one-host boundary.

construction_spec.function: Describe one bare child as physically small.
host_classes: exact pair: contact child plus contact small
restrictions: No other noun or property word is licensed.
No definiteness, plurality, possession, comparison, intensity, or predicate use.
counterexamples: katan yeled is invalid in this construction.
Interpreting small as young or dear is invalid.

change_note: Licensed only yeled katan as an invariant postnominal physical-size phrase.

senses.definition: Postpose contact yaxad to one of four declared first-plural eating clauses so every indexed subject member jointly performs that activity.

grammatical_features: The host clause is complete before yaxad is added.
Clusivity remains entirely on the predicate.

translation: The construction asserts co-participation, not merely temporal overlap.
grammar: Yaxad adds no new participant and is neither the ordinary coordinator wə- nor a comitative or reciprocal marker.
design: A Hebrew-derived communal frame scopes over a regional person-and-valency predicate, realizing the co-parent goal inside one everyday clause.

operations.description: Postpose yaxad after a complete admitted inclusive or exclusive bread/fruit clause.

formation.design_alignment: Turns the song's togetherness into explicit mixed grammar rather than an English-only note.

provenance.generation_note: Codex manually defined the scope, order, four hosts, and negative boundaries.

construction_spec.function: Mark joint participation by the members of an already indexed first-plural subject.
restrictions: No separate comitative NP, reciprocal reading, clause coordination, simultaneity-only reading, TAM, or narrative relation.
counterexamples: yaxad cannot replace wə- between clauses.
A singular clause cannot host yaxad here.
Yaxad before the predicate is outside the construction.

change_note: Created a four-host postclausal yaxad construction for shared eating.

english: eat in or at a declared setting

senses.definition: Append one declared static locative phrase to one of four complete eating clauses as the setting of the event.

idiomatic: eat in a house or at a table

grammatical_features: The object remains immediately after the predicate and the setting follows the complete core clause.
The locative describes where the event occurs, not a goal, source, path, or possessed place.

translation: Bayitənk remains a general static dwelling location and does not itself mean home, our home, or indoors.
grammar: This exact construction does not generalize every static locative to every predicate.
design: The sentence now combines regional valency, Hebrew food vocabulary, and regional locative morphology on Hebrew household nouns.

operations.description: Append the revision-pinned static phrase after the complete objectful clause in one of four declared combinations.

formation.formation_process: Manual closed composition of four eating clauses with two existing static settings.
formation.design_alignment: Builds a richer mixed ordinary clause while keeping possession, direction, and general adjunct productivity unresolved.

provenance.generation_note: Codex manually selected all four clause-setting combinations and their scope boundaries.

construction_spec.function: State the static setting of one admitted eating event.
ordering: finite predicate with any required lexical subject
restrictions: The setting is not possessed, plural, directional, definite, or incorporated.
No arrival, source, path, duration, habituality, tense, or narrative sequence is contributed.
counterexamples: bayitənk cannot replace the food object.
el bayit and min bayit are not static settings here.
The construction does not express our homes.

change_note: Licensed four exact objectful eating clauses with house or table event settings.
